name: Macha Besara
subtitle: rohu steaks in a hot, sour ground-mustard gravy, the Sunday fish curry of coastal Odisha

ingredients.qty: 600g rohu or katla, cut into 2cm-thick steaks
ingredients.note: any firm freshwater fish on the bone

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, soaked in warm water 20 minutes

ingredients.note: 1 tsp for rubbing the fish, 1/2 tsp for the gravy
4 for frying the fish, 1 for the gravy

prepNotes: Rub the fish steaks with 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp salt and leave 15 minutes at room temperature. This firms the flesh so it does not break in the pan.
Soak the mustard seeds 20 minutes, then grind with 3 garlic cloves, 2 green chillies and a pinch of salt to a fine paste with 4 tbsp water.
Pat the fish dry just before frying. Wet fish sticks to the pan and tears when you turn it.

steps.text: Grind the soaked mustard, garlic, green chillies and a pinch of salt to a smooth paste with 4 tbsp water. Set aside.
Heat 4 tbsp mustard oil in a kadhai until it smokes. Fry the turmeric-rubbed fish in one layer, 3 minutes a side, until a light crust forms.
steps.tip: Do not move the fish for the first 3 minutes. It releases from the pan on its own once the crust sets.

steps.text: Lift the fish out onto a plate. Pour off all but about 1 tbsp of the oil.
Add the panch phoron to the hot oil and let it crackle 20 seconds, then add the sliced garlic and 2 slit green chillies.
Add the chopped tomato with 1/2 tsp turmeric, the chilli powder and salt. Cook 6 minutes, mashing, until the tomato collapses and the oil separates.
Pour in the water and bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
Drop the flame to its lowest and stir in the mustard paste. Simmer uncovered 5 minutes without letting it boil.
steps.tip: A hard boil after the mustard goes in makes the gravy bitter. Keep it barely trembling.

steps.text: Slide the fried fish back in, spoon gravy over each piece, and simmer 4 minutes more.
Take off the heat, scatter the coriander leaves and rest 10 minutes before serving. The fish keeps absorbing gravy as it stands.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat on the lowest flame in a wide pan without stirring, tilting the pan to baste the fish instead; stirring breaks the steaks apart.
